target.title: fix(auto-reply): keep export tree truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The exported session HTML tree preview must truncate long node text without breaking emoji or other supplementary-plane characters, and it must not scan or allocate the entire message just to keep the first 100 preview characters. The first code-point-safe implementation used `Array.from(s)` over the full message text, which could make large session exports stall or allocate heavily.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up replaces full-string materialization with a bounded `for...of` scan that stops at the preview budget and slices by the resulting UTF-16 offset. This preserves code-point-safe truncation and the existing `...` suffix while avoiding full traversal/allocation of large message content.

## User Impact

`/export-session` HTML tree previews keep emoji boundaries intact and remain responsive when a session contains very large message text.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head after bot follow-up: `2c85cc6104a`
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.js src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.js src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts`: no formatting target because these export-html files are ignored by oxfmt in this checkout, not a formatting failure
- Real-browser proof: generated a session export HTML with a tree message shaped as `99 x chars + U+1F600 + 500000 y chars`, opened the generated file in headless system Chrome through Playwright, and captured `.tree-content` from the rendered page:

```json
{
  "text": "user: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx??...",
  "codePoints": 109,
  "containsEmoji": true,
  "emojiHex": "1f600",
  "containsEllipsisSuffix": true,
  "containsLongTail": false,
  "loneSurrogate": false
}
```

- Local proof artifact generated but not committed: `.tmp-proof-106400/large-tree-export.html` and `.tmp-proof-106400/large-tree-export.png`.
- Regression coverage now includes the original emoji-boundary tree preview plus a large-message tree preview that asserts the long tail does not leak into the rendered preview.

Known proof gap: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "tree node truncation"` did not return output before the local 180s timeout in this Windows worktree, so the current update does not claim a fresh local Vitest pass. CI should provide the full test signal for the pushed head.

target.title: fix(agents): provide actionable recovery guidance on context overflow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs exec commands producing large output (e.g. `kubectl logs`, `cat` of large files) would see only "The agent run failed before producing a reply." — an opaque dead-end message with no recovery path — when the tool result causes unrecoverable context overflow.

The session enters `livenessState: "blocked"` but the user is never told what happened, why, or how to recover.

Related issue: #106204

## Why This Change Was Made

Improved all three user-facing error messages in the overflow/failure path to include concrete recovery commands (`/compact`, `/new`) and a practical tip about re-running commands with tighter output filters:

- `run.ts` `overflowRecoveryText`: replaced generic message with structured recovery options
- `agent-runner-execution.ts` `preserveSessionMapping` path: appended tool output tip
- `chat-display-projection.ts` `GATEWAY_ASSISTANT_ERROR_FALLBACK_TEXT`: added `/compact` and `/new` hints

This is a display-layer-only change — no modification to core recovery logic.

## User Impact

Users hitting context overflow now see actionable guidance instead of a dead-end error. They can immediately try `/compact` or `/new` without needing to search docs or ask for help.

## Evidence

- `npx oxlint@1.72.0` on all 3 modified source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `npx vitest run server-methods.test.ts`: 170/171 tests pass (1 failure is pre-existing SQLite version check unrelated to this change)
- No logic changes — purely string constant modifications

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(config): prune cron-run descendant sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed cron run cleanup can leave stale descendant session registry rows behind, such as subagent or thread rows under `agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<runId>:...`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isCronRunSessionKey()` already treats cron-run descendants as cron-run session keys, but session registry maintenance only matched exact `cron:<job>:run:<runId>` rows. This caused stale descendants to be preserved as ordinary sessions.

This change aligns session registry maintenance with the existing cron-run session key classification.

## User Impact

Cron run session registry maintenance now prunes stale completed cron-run descendants while still preserving descendants for currently running cron jobs and preserving ordinary non-cron sessions.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- Added focused regression coverage in
  `src/config/sessions/session-registry-maintenance.test.ts`.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: no actionable regressions found.

### Local SQLite Runtime Proof

In addition to the committed regression test, I ran a temporary local runtime
harness against an isolated SQLite-backed session registry. This was not a
mocked store and did not use any personal OpenClaw state.

The temporary harness used production APIs only:

- `replaceSessionEntry()` to persist the SQLite-backed registry rows;
- `beginSessionWorkAdmission()` to register an active runtime admission;
- `runSessionRegistryMaintenanceForStore({ apply: true, ... })` to execute the
  production maintenance path; and
- `listSessionEntries()` to read the persisted rows before and after apply.

The committed regression test provides the reviewable and CI-reproducible
version of this scenario. The terminal transcript below is supplementary local
runtime evidence from the same production persistence and maintenance APIs.

Raw terminal output:

```text
PR #105633 real SQLite maintenance proof
before (6): ["agent:main:cron:active-job:run:active-run:subagent:worker","agent:main:cron:done-job:run:old-run","agent:main:cron:done-job:run:old-run:subagent:worker","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run:thread:reply","agent:main:subagent:ordinary-worker"]
result: {"afterCount":4,"beforeCount":6,"preservedRunning":2,"pruned":2}
after (4): ["agent:main:cron:active-job:run:active-run:subagent:worker","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run:thread:reply","agent:main:subagent:ordinary-worker"]

✓ 1 test passed
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex for codebase navigation, implementation, and review. I reviewed the final implementation and tests and understand the behavior change.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): keep export tree truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The exported session HTML tree preview must truncate long node text without breaking emoji or other supplementary-plane characters, and it must not scan or allocate the entire message just to keep the first 100 preview characters. The first code-point-safe implementation used `Array.from(s)` over the full message text, which could make large session exports stall or allocate heavily.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up replaces full-string materialization with a bounded `for...of` scan that stops at the preview budget and slices by the resulting UTF-16 offset. This preserves code-point-safe truncation and the existing `...` suffix while avoiding full traversal/allocation of large message content.

## User Impact

`/export-session` HTML tree previews keep emoji boundaries intact and remain responsive when a session contains very large message text.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head after bot follow-up: `2c85cc6104a`
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.js src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts`: pass

- Real-browser proof: generated a session export HTML with a tree message shaped as `99 x chars + U+1F600 + 500000 y chars`, opened the generated file in headless system Chrome through Playwright, and captured `.tree-content` from the rendered page:

```json
{
  "text": "user: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx??...",
  "codePoints": 109,
  "containsEmoji": true,
  "emojiHex": "1f600",
  "containsEllipsisSuffix": true,
  "containsLongTail": false,

}
```

- Regression coverage now includes the original emoji-boundary tree preview plus a large-message tree preview that asserts the long tail does not leak into the rendered preview.

Known proof gap: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "tree node truncation"` did not return output before the local 180s timeout in this Windows worktree, so the current update does not claim a fresh local Vitest pass. # PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`

- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root-work set to the direct-stop path. The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll (not `.unref()`) so the timer keeps the event loop alive. target.title: fix(feishu): pass timeoutMs through app-registration guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: exported `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts`
- Production caller path: `beginAppRegistration` → `postRegistration` → `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`

target.title: feat(mcp): requester-scoped MCP server connections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106229. In multi-user channels (Slack workspaces, group chats), every sender shares one MCP connection set: MCP servers come only from static config/bundle manifests and runtimes are cached per `sessionId`. Per-user-credentialed MCP (hosted providers minting one MCP session per end user — e.g. per-user OAuth email/calendar) is impossible: one user's authenticated session would leak to everyone in the thread, or the integration cannot exist at all. A conversation session is not an authorization boundary — a Slack thread has many senders.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic, provider-agnostic core primitive; all provider logic stays in plugins:

- **New plugin API:** `api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver({ serverName, resolve })`. Server *identity* stays static (`mcp.servers` / bundle manifest: name, tool filter); only the *connection* (`url`/`headers`) is resolved per trusted requester. `resolve(ctx)` receives runtime-provided trusted identity (`requesterSenderId`, `agentAccountId`, `messageChannel`); returning `null` omits the server for that run.
- **Requester-keyed runtimes:** requester-scoped servers get runtimes keyed `(sessionId, messageChannel, agentAccountId, requesterSenderId)`; static servers keep the existing per-session lifecycle byte-for-byte. Sessions with no registered resolvers are entirely unchanged.
- **Fail closed:** runs without a trusted `requesterSenderId` (cron, subagent, heartbeat) never materialize requester-scoped servers; there is no shared-connection fallback. `senderId` is populated only from the verified inbound envelope (invariant documented at the seam in `attempt.ts`).
- **Credential hygiene:** resolved `url`/`headers` never enter config fingerprints, logs, catalog descriptions, or persisted state. Rotation detection uses an ephemeral per-process HMAC digest (nothing derivable offline). Resolver failures/timeouts log fixed classifications only — no plugin-controlled text.
- **Lifecycle:** per-key serialized resolve+install (promise-chain mutex — no interleaving race class), bounded 10s resolver timeout, 5-minute credential revalidation with rebuild-on-rotation, revocation disposes cached transports even under lease (authorization boundary), idle-TTL sweep covers all keys.
- **Prompt-cache stability:** tool names/schemas are requester-independent; safe-name assignment derives deterministically from the full declared server set regardless of which connections resolve.

Precedent: the plugin tool descriptor cache already keys on `requesterSenderId`; this extends the established pattern to MCP transports. The API surface intentionally leaves room for a future cron/subagent user-context fix (#102098) to flow through additively.

**Note for reviewers (surface changes):** no new `openclaw.json` keys or env vars. Plugin SDK gains one registration method + 3 public type exports; `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` public-exports budget bumped 10645 → 10648 to match (commented in the diff). `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` regenerated per the check's documented flow.

## User Impact

Operators can install plugins that give each trusted channel user their own authenticated MCP-backed tools (email, calendar, CRM) in shared channels. Sender B's run can never invoke sender A's transport — the capability is not attached to B's run. Existing configurations see zero behavior change. Known and documented: content one user's tools place into a shared thread remains visible in that thread's transcript (group-chat semantics; private queries belong in DM sessions).

## Evidence

- Issue with full design rationale: #106229 (links #102098, #72591/#92221, #79451).
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox + local focused runs): `pnpm check:changed` lanes green (format, SDK baseline, SDK exports, surface budget, lint); `tsgo` + `tsgo:test` exit 0; focused suites `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `mcp-connection-resolver`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names`, `agent-bundle-mcp-filter` — 100+ tests green.
- Six rounds of structured adversarial review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) drove the hardening above: resolver timeout/error containment, revocation-disposes-under-lease, per-key serialization replacing three interim concurrency guards (net −70 LOC in the manager), HMAC digest instead of plain credential hash, constant catalog descriptions, SSE alias preservation, lease aggregation for requester-only sessions, safe-name-map fingerprint participation.
- Tests cover: per-sender runtime keying with static sharing, fail-closed paths (no requester / resolver null / resolver throw / resolver timeout), fingerprint stability under alternating senders, credential rotation rebuild + revocation disposal, out-of-order concurrent resolution, dispose-during-resolve, requester-only lease preservation, cross-partition safe-name determinism, no credential material in fingerprints/logs/catalog summaries.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: gateway MCP-app reconstruction lacks requester context (scoped servers stay fail-closed absent there); cron/subagent requester context is #102098.

target.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
target.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` (or with `--agent` on the parent `models` command) would silently read and write the global `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain instead of the named agent's own fallback chain. `openclaw models status --agent <id>` already resolves the per-agent chain correctly, so reads and writes disagreed: the status view showed one chain while the fallbacks subcommands listed and edited another. The `image-fallbacks` group silently ignored `--agent` too.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `models fallbacks` subcommands now thread `--agent` the same way `models status` does (via `resolveModelAgentOption`), validate the id with the same `resolveKnownAgentId` guard `models status` uses (unknown ids error instead of silently editing global defaults), read the agent's own fallbacks override when it has one, and write through a new `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks` helper that mirrors the existing `setAgentEffectiveModelPrimary` pattern (mutate the agent's `agents.list[]` entry when it owns an override, otherwise update `agents.defaults.model`). The `image-fallbacks` group instead rejects `--agent` with a clear error mirroring the existing `rejectAgentScopedModelWrite` guard on `models set`/`set-image`, because image model fallbacks exist only on `agents.defaults.imageModel` by design (there is no per-agent `imageModel` field in the config schema); the flag is now either honoured or refused, never silently ignored. The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) stays global in all cases; only the fallback list itself is agent-scoped.

## User Impact

Operators of multi-agent deployments can now inspect and edit a single agent's fallback chain from the CLI: `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` operates on that agent's chain when the agent has its own model override, and on the global defaults otherwise (matching what `models status --agent <id>` reports). Without `--agent`, behaviour is unchanged. `models image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` now fails fast with an explanatory message instead of silently editing global defaults.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` cover `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks`: agent-override writes go to the agent entry (defaults untouched), no-override writes go to defaults, clearing in place, and an agent with an explicit primary but no fallbacks yet.
- New CLI wiring tests in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` cover `--agent` forwarding for fallbacks list/add/remove/clear (parent and subcommand flag placement), the unchanged no-agent path, rejection of parent `--agent` for all four `image-fallbacks` subcommands, and the unchanged no-agent image path.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the terminal-main reconciliation gate silently resets a healthy main session on the next inbound message after idle. The gate compares transcript mtime against entry `updatedAt`, and a post-run transcript append (delivery receipt, maintenance write, tool output) creates a margin of tens of milliseconds where `mtime > updatedAt`. Once this condition is true, `freshEntry` becomes false regardless of the configured reset policy — even with a 365-day idle window. The user's session "wakes up blank" with no log line and no error.

Concrete scenario: session completes normally (`status: "done"`, `endedAt` set), a delivery note touches the transcript file 93 ms after `updatedAt` is written, and the next inbound message rolls the session over. Observed on three consecutive days after idle periods.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal-main transcript gate (`hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistry`) exists to detect zombie sessions whose transcript was modified after the registry marked them done. But the gate fired for sessions still fresh under the configured reset policy — a false positive.

The fix: only honor the gate when the session is already stale under the reset policy. If the entry is still fresh (within the idle/daily window), a touched transcript is not a zombie — the session is healthy and should not be rolled over.

Two call sites patched:
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` — `freshEntry` computation for the auto-reply admission path
- `src/agents/command/session.ts` — `fresh` computation for the command/CLI resolve-session path

The logic is symmetric: compute policy freshness first, then apply the terminal gate only when the result is already `!fresh`. When `policyFresh` is true, the gate is a no-op (the session survives).

## User Impact

Sessions with long idle windows (hours to days) no longer silently reset after a post-run transcript touch. The first message after idle preserves the existing session context. Sessions genuinely expired under the reset policy continue to roll over normally.

## Evidence

## Summary

`streamSessionTranscriptLines` and `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` used bare `catch { return; }` blocks that silently swallowed all filesystem errors. Replace them with `catch (err) { transcriptLog.warn(...); return; }`.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/config/sessions/transcript-stream.ts`, both streaming functions catch `fs.promises.stat` / `fs.promises.open` errors and silently return empty iterators. While an empty iterator is the correct contract for missing files, other errors (permission denied, I/O error) should be visible in diagnostics.

## Root Cause

The functions were designed to return an empty iterator when the file cannot be read, but the empty catch blocks discarded all diagnostic information.

## Why This Fix

Same pattern as [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) and [#106385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106385) — `createSubsystemLogger` + `formatErrorMessage(err)`.

## Evidence

- **Before**: EACCES error silently swallowed → empty iterator, no diagnostic
- **After**: EACCES error logged → `[transcript-stream] Failed to stat transcript /root/nonexistent-transcript.jsonl: EACCES: permission denied`

## Real Behavior Proof

### After (with fix)

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render with grapheme-leading name:
  - Real Lit component renders with textContent = "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + Component test
- Target test files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji initial, joined emoji grapheme, flag grapheme, skin-tone grapheme, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path with surrogate pair preservation
  - Selector: grapheme cluster preserved in real Lit component DOM render
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact grapheme boundary at both helper and component level, plus browser compatibility path.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit) and later `codePointAt(0)` (first code point), neither of which respects grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No grapheme-aware initial derivation; agent selector had a separate inconsistent fallback; no Intl.Segmenter feature detection for browser compatibility.

target.title: fix(agents): reject aborted foreground exec with AbortError
target.body:
Closes #105681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where canceling a foreground `exec` tool call via the agent `AbortSignal` still fulfilled the tool result as a normal process exit/failure payload. The agent manager could treat the tool as completed instead of aborted, so cancellation did not cleanly surface as an abort error on the tool path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Foreground abort already kills the child process, but the wrapper promise still resolved through `buildExecForegroundResult` after the process exited. This change records caller abort for foreground runs, clears any armed yield timer before kill (so the timer cannot resolve a "running" result first), waits for the existing process finalization promise, then rejects with the signal reason or a canonical `AbortError`. Backgrounded/yielded sessions remain detached and are not killed by the tool-turn abort. Timeouts and ordinary non-abort process failures still use the existing normalized result path.

**Fix quality check:** compatibility — no config/API surface change; performance — O(1) flag/timer clear on abort only; usability — abort surfaces as `AbortError` instead of a misleading completed tool result; security — no trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

When an operator or agent runtime cancels a foreground bash/exec tool mid-run, the tool promise rejects with `AbortError` after process finalization instead of returning a successful-looking failed/exit tool payload. Backgrounded process sessions are unchanged.

target.title: fix(mattermost): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildMattermostWebSocketClientOptions` as the single production options surface (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Default Mattermost `WebSocket` factory consumes that builder.
- Regressions observe that production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control to `runWithReconnect`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError` / close before open), allowing the reconnect loop to continue.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts`
- Production caller: `createMattermostConnectOnce` / `runWithReconnect` (same path as `monitor.ts`)
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`)
- Regression: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`
- ClawSweeper follow-ups addressed: production-wiring coverage + standalone timeout→reconnect output (including full 30s default-factory floor)

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text

 ✓ ... > fails connect when the websocket handshake never completes 203ms

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.05s
```

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**

```bash
PROOF_MODE=short node /tmp/openclaw-mattermost-handshake-proof/standalone.mjs
PROOF_MODE=default-factory node /tmp/openclaw-mattermost-handshake-proof/standalone.mjs
```

**Before fix:**
Default Mattermost `WebSocket` options had no `handshakeTimeout`, so `createMattermostConnectOnce` could wait indefinitely for `open`.

**After fix:**
Production builder wires `handshakeTimeout: 30000` into the default factory. Against a TCP peer that accepts but never upgrades:

1. Short standalone run (200ms stand-in): timeout then reconnect attempt.
2. Default-factory floor (30_000 ms): first attempt fails at ~30s, reconnect schedules, second attempt also times out.
